title: Managing Dependencies
description: Combine package managers, subtrees, and submodules to manage project dependencies effectively.

data.text: Modern projects use a mix of package managers (npm, NuGet, pip), Git subtrees, and submodules to manage dependencies. Understanding when to use each approach keeps your project maintainable and your dependencies up to date.

items: **Package managers** (npm, NuGet, pip): Standard libraries with published versions
**Git subtrees**: Vendored libraries you need to customize
**Git submodules**: Shared libraries maintained in separate repositories
**Lock files** (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, package.json): Pin transitive dependency versions

data.text: Choose a versioning strategy based on how you consume the dependency. Published libraries use semantic versioning. Internal libraries may use Git tags or commit SHAs. Vendored code uses the subtree or submodule commit pointer.

data.title: Versioning strategies by dependency type
data.code:
# Published library (npm):
# package.json: "lodash": "^4.17.21"
npm install

# Vendored library (subtree):
# Records the external commit SHA

git subtree add --prefix=vendor/lib https://github.com/example/lib.git main --squash

# Shared library (submodule):
# Records the external commit SHA

git submodule add https://github.com/example/lib.git external/lib

data.text: Different dependency types require different update commands. Package managers have built-in update commands. Subtrees use git subtree pull. Submodules require entering the submodule and pulling.

data.title: Update all dependency types
data.code:
# Update npm dependencies
npm update

# Update subtree
git subtree pull --prefix=vendor/lib \
  https://github.com/example/lib.git main --squash

# Update submodule
external/lib$ git checkout main
external/lib$ git pull origin main
cd ..
git add external/lib
git commit -m "chore: update lib submodule"

data.text: Lock files (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, package.json) record the exact versions of all transitive dependencies. Commit lock files to Git so every developer and CI uses identical dependency versions.

data.title: Always commit lock files
data.text: Lock files guarantee reproducible builds. Without them, npm install can resolve to different versions depending on when it runs, causing 'works on my machine' bugs.
Regularly audit dependencies for security vulnerabilities and outdated packages. Use npm audit, npm outdated, or GitHub Dependabot to stay informed.

data.title: Audit dependencies
data.code:
# Check for known vulnerabilities
npm audit

# Fix automatically where possible
npm audit fix

# List outdated packages
npm outdated

# Update a specific package
npm update lodash

# Use Dependabot on GitHub for automated updates
# Enable in repository Settings → Dependabot

data.text: Internal libraries (shared across teams) may use submodules or a private npm registry. External libraries (third-party) use public npm or NuGet. Vendored code uses subtrees when you need to customize the dependency.

items: **Internal libraries**: Use a private npm registry or submodule
**External libraries**: Use public npm, NuGet, or pip
**Vendored code**: Use subtrees when you need to customize the dependency
**Shared infrastructure**: Use submodules when multiple projects depend on the same code

items.question: Can I use a monorepo instead of submodules?
items.answer: Yes. Tools like Nx, Turborepo, and Lerna let you manage multiple packages in a single repository, avoiding the complexity of submodules entirely.

items.question: Should I commit node_modules?
items.answer: No. Commit package.json and package-lock.json. Use npm install to regenerate node_modules. The only exception is when deploying to environments without npm.

items.question: How do I handle private dependencies in CI?
items.answer: Use CI secrets for npm tokens or SSH keys for Git submodules. Never commit credentials to Git.

items.question: Can Dependabot update submodules?
items.answer: Dependabot does not currently support submodule updates. Use a custom script or GitHub Actions to keep submodules current.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use package managers for standard libraries with published versions
Use subtrees for vendored code you need to customize
Use submodules for shared libraries with separate release cycles
Commit lock files to guarantee reproducible builds
Audit dependencies regularly with npm audit and Dependabot
